key_insight: The paper argues that reference-policy KL regularization can misfire in group policy optimization because KL and reward signals interact unevenly, and it proposes calibrating within-group updates using conditional KL instead of applying KL as a fixed penalty.
engineering_relevance: For RLHF-style training, this suggests that stable policy improvement may require length-aware, group-relative calibration rather than a blanket KL term, especially when rewards are clipped or nearly tied.
method: Identify seven failure modes where KL either persists when it should vanish or dominates due to length/token imbalance.
Define Zero-Sum Calibrated Policy Optimization (ZCPO) to measure relative drift with conditional KL.
Use that drift to calibrate within-group reward coefficients and fold them into the base surrogate objective.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical reasoning experiments and ablations that support the proposed ZCPO design in the authors' setting.
watch_item: Conditional-KL calibration may be sensitive to how groups are formed and to response-length/tokenization choices, so implementation details could change the observed benefit.
paper_title: When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization
